jobs.title: Federal Product Marketing Manager
jobs.description:
Backed by leading Silicon Valley investors, Peregrine helps public safety organizations, state and local and governments, federal agencies , and private-sector institutions address society’s challenges with unprecedented speed and accuracy. Our AI-enabled platform turns siloed and disconnected data into operational intelligence — instantly surfacing mission-critical information to empower better, faster decisions that improve outcomes at every touchpoint. Today Peregrine supports hundreds of customers across 30+ states and two countries, serving more than 125 million people — and we’re amplifying our impact as we expand into the enterprise and internationally.

The Role

Federal is Peregrine's next market, and you will be its founding product marketer, reporting to the VP of Product Marketing. Peregrine's platform runs in production across hundreds of state and local agencies. In federal law enforcement missions, that work translates directly. In adjacent segments, this role runs the discovery to find it. The role is full-stack: positioning, embedded work with capture and pre-sales, and early campaign testing. There is no federal marketing foundation yet. You will build it, in the field, inside live pursuits.

In this role, you will…

- Own federal positioning and messaging, including translating proven state and local law enforcement work for federal missions, and a clear articulation of how we earn trust: auditability, access controls, and accountable AI.

- Run discovery in unproven segments: win-loss, buyer research, and messaging hypotheses tested through live pursuits.

- Feed product marketing messaging into the capture-led win strategy for pursuits (e.g., positioning, competitive counters, and holding every claim to what's proven across briefings, RFI and sources sought responses, and proposals).

- Build the pre-solicitation content set to influence acquisitions at scale (capability briefings, mission white papers, industry day materials).

- Arm pre-sales teams with first-call narratives, demo storylines, and objection handling.

- Partner with growth team to deliver early test campaigns, including defining segments, identifying and engaging the right external industry partners and events, and hands-on production of market-facing assets.

- Package deployment proof into federal-ready evidence: case studies, references, outcome data cleared for public use.

- Feed pursuit and campaign learning back into positioning and product.

What you’ll bring

- Authorship that changed an outcome: a positioning document that moved a deal, a requirement, or an executive decision.

- Working knowledge of the federal procurement lifecycle and the compliance frameworks federal buyers evaluate against.

- 7+ years in product marketing or adjacent go-to-market roles, including 3+ years marketing or selling technology to the US federal government.

- Range across the full product marketing stack: positioning, pursuit support, enablement, and campaign execution.

- Comfort treating an unmapped segment as a research problem with a deadline.

- Judgment on when a claim is proven versus promising, built working alongside technical field teams.

- Adept at operating across two registers: technical depth for program offices, plain language for public surfaces.

What success looks like

- You can make the federal case yourself: in a program office briefing, you deliver the argument for why the mission needs what Peregrine builds, in the buyer's terms, and it holds when they push back.

- Capture and pre-sales reach for your positioning unprompted. The language in capability briefings, RFI responses, and first-call decks traces back to you.

- Positioning lands before solicitations drop: win strategy documents and requirement language reflect framing you wrote.

- Adjacent-segment discovery ends in decisions: documented pursue-or-pass calls grounded in win-loss and buyer research.

- Federal claims survive contracting, legal, and security review without being walked back.

- Deployment proof is federal-ready: cleared case studies and references that pre-sales uses without a legal review on every send.

- Capture and pre-sales pull you into pursuits early, and the state and local teams open their deployment proof to you.

You might thrive in this role if…

- You've built a marketing motion from nothing and want to do it again.

- You go to the source: program offices, contracting officers, the agents and analysts in the field. Reports come second.

- You form a point of view from thin data and revise it when the evidence moves.

- You say what's proven and no more, even when a pursuit is on the clock.

- You want to be in the room: onsite in DC, at industry days, alongside capture and pre-sales.

- The mission is concrete for you: you can name the agencies, the people in them, and the problems you want this work to serve.

Annual Salary + Benefits + Equity (if applicable) + Bonus (if applicable)
$157,000 — $202,000 USD

Actual compensation is influenced by a wide array of factors including but not limited to skill set, level of experience, certifications or licenses, and specific work location. Information on the benefits offered is  here .

Peregrine Technologies is committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. We celebrate diversity and are a proud equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status.

jobs.title: Product Operations Manager
jobs.description:
Backed by leading Silicon Valley investors, Peregrine helps public safety organizations, state and local and governments, federal agencies , and private-sector institutions address society’s challenges with unprecedented speed and accuracy. Our AI-enabled platform turns siloed and disconnected data into operational intelligence — instantly surfacing mission-critical information to empower better, faster decisions that improve outcomes at every touchpoint. Today Peregrine supports hundreds of customers across 30+ states and two countries, serving more than 125 million people — and we’re amplifying our impact as we expand into the enterprise and internationally.

Role

As Peregrine's Product organization scales, we're investing in our first dedicated Product Operations hire. This role will help define how Product operates—from how we measure success, to how we launch features, to how we continuously improve the way we work.

You'll partner closely with Product Managers, Engineering, Design, Data Science, Customer Delivery, Sales Enablement, and Training to build the systems, metrics, and operational rhythms that allow the team to move faster with greater confidence. Rather than owning a product roadmap yourself, you'll own the operating model that enables every roadmap to be executed more effectively.

This is a high-ownership, high-visibility role for someone who enjoys bringing structure to ambiguity, loves solving operational problems, and wants to help shape how a growing product organization scales.

What You'll Own

📊 Metrics & Reporting

- Curate and maintain Peregrine's core product metrics library — definitions, owners, and calculation logic

- Own the data and dashboards behind Monthly Business Reviews and quarterly/annual planning cycles

- Validate metric correctness as new features ship; add instrumentation directly or work with engineers to add

- Work across a toolset including Amplitude, Datadog, and dogfood our own product

🚀 Launch & Rollout Coordination

- Drive the operational plan for betas and broader rollouts and launches — tracking readiness across Training, CA, Sales Enablement, DS, Marketing, and Documentation

- Maintain a shared view of launch status, exit criteria, and early signal against success metrics

- Run structured post-launch retrospectives and circulate findings to the PM team

🧭 PM Team Enablement

- Maintain the PM team's operational rhythm: OKR tracking, roadmap tooling hygiene

- Build and maintain playbooks so feature onboarding and recurring processes don't rely on tribal knowledge

- Ensure feedback loops from early adopters and EAP participants are closed and documented

What We're Looking For

- 4+ years of experience in product operations, business operations, strategy & analytics, statistics, or a PM-adjacent role in enterprise SaaS

- Strong analytical skills — comfortable in Python, SQL, Amplitude, or similar tools; you can build a dashboard and also interrogate whether it's measuring the right thing

- AI-forward thinking — how do you leverage the latest AI tools to automate and scale yourself and your workflows

- Experience coordinating cross-functional launches or programs with multiple stakeholders

- Clear, concise written communication — you write docs that people actually read and are strong at synthesizing data and trends

- Comfort with ambiguity; able to identify what structure is missing and create it without waiting to be asked

Nice to Have

- Familiarity with public sector compliance requirements

- Prior exposure to data science/engineering or instrumentation pipelines

jobs.title: Technical Product Marketing Lead
jobs.description:
Backed by leading Silicon Valley investors, Peregrine helps public safety organizations, state and local and governments, federal agencies , and private-sector institutions address society’s challenges with unprecedented speed and accuracy. Our AI-enabled platform turns siloed and disconnected data into operational intelligence — instantly surfacing mission-critical information to empower better, faster decisions that improve outcomes at every touchpoint. Today Peregrine supports hundreds of customers across 30+ states and two countries, serving more than 125 million people — and we’re amplifying our impact as we expand into the enterprise and internationally.

The role

Peregrine's value lives below the surface. We unify dozens of disconnected data sources, resolve entities, preserve context, and ground AI in that unified picture. The visible product is a small fraction of the work that drives customer outcomes. The harder, more durable value lives in the integration layer underneath. This is a builder role for someone excited to make that layer legible, defensible, and competitive for audiences ranging from public safety operators to federal evaluators to commercial technical buyers. The work starts from technical depth; everything else in the role builds on it. Peregrine is creating a category without established head-to-head competitors, so a core part of this role is teaching the market what to evaluate.

You will be the founding Technical Product Marketer, reporting to the VP of Product Marketing. There is no technical marketing foundation yet; you will build it from scratch for prospects, analysts, and sellers, and Solutions Marketing will adapt it for specific verticals and audiences. This role owns product positioning, messaging, and competitive narrative across the platform: what Peregrine claims, how those claims are defended, and what the market learns to evaluate.

In this role you will...

- Own technical positioning and messaging for the core platform: data unification, entity resolution, AI grounding, integration architecture, and the operational AI layer built on that foundation.

- Demystify the category itself. Build the first-principles content that explains why unifying operational data, resolving entities, and grounding AI are genuinely hard problems, why common approaches fall short, and what an architecture built for this work actually requires.

- Build the technical content library the rest of marketing and sales depends on: technical whitepapers, architecture briefs, security and compliance content, and AI substantiation that holds up under public, legal, and political scrutiny.

- Turn competitive technical intelligence into asymmetric sales tools and teardowns that hold up against horizontal data platforms, operational AI platforms, and AI point solutions.

- Contribute product-led narratives to high-visibility launches, with focus on the technical proof points that make each launch credible.

What you'll bring

- 5+ years of work experience across engineering and product marketing. A technical foundation is required: a computer science or related degree, an early-career engineering role, or equivalent built depth. You can read a spec, work through a data model, and defend an architectural claim to our CTO.

- Product marketing experience in B2B SaaS, AI, or data infrastructure. You have authored positioning where none existed and built competitive teardowns that moved real deals.

- Management consulting experience can add supporting depth in structured problem decomposition, analytical rigor, and the ability to learn complex domains fast. However it does not substitute for the technical foundation.

- Exceptional writing. You can produce technical content that holds up to a technical reader and translates cleanly for a non-technical one.

- Comfort moving between deep technical conversations with engineers and business outcome conversations with executives, without losing either audience.

What success looks like

- Build a working mental model of Peregrine's platform, deep enough to defend technical claims independently across the stack.

- Sellers reach for your content unprompted in deal cycles.

- Peregrine has a defensible technical narrative against horizontal data platforms, operational AI platforms, and AI point solutions that sellers and prospects can articulate consistently.

- Peregrine's AI claims hold up under technical and security reviews and public scrutiny.

- Build trusted partnerships with Product, Engineering, Forward Deployed Engineering, Solutions Engineering and Solutions Marketing.

- Influence the product-led narrative for major launches.

You might thrive in this role if...

- You started in engineering or technical product work and deliberately moved toward the market side.

- You're curious about how things actually work and unsatisfied with surface explanations.

- You're energized by translation work: taking complex technical depth and making it clear, defensible, and competitive.

- You're energized by category-shaping work, not just category-winning work. You'd rather define what "good" looks like than out-position named competitors on established criteria.

- Writing is a craft for you and you care about getting the details right.

- You move between technical and non-technical audiences without losing either.

- You want to own a layer of the product story that compounds over time, rather than running one launch after another.

- You're drawn to mission-driven work and the chance to support public safety, emergency response, and government agencies with real operational impact.
